title: Finland – Business services: law, marketing, consulting, recruitment, printing and security – Soveltuvuus- ja potentiaaliarviointipalvelut
description: Hankinnan kohteena ovat Tilaajan tarpeisiin tuotettavat soveltuvuus- ja potentiaaliarviointipalvelut. Palveluja käytetään Tilaajan sisäisten ja ulkoisten rekrytointien tukena sekä henkilöstön kehittämisessä. Palveluntuottajan tulee pystyä tuottamaan arviointeja eri henkilöstöryhmille, kuten johtajille, esihenkilöille / päälliköille ja asiantuntijoille. Palvelun tavoitteena on tuottaa Tilaajalle luotettavaa, objektiivista ja tutkimusnäyttöön perustuvaa arviointitietoa päätöksenteon tueksi. Arviointien tulee tukea laadukasta rekrytointia ja henkilöstön kehittämistä. Hankinta sisältää seuraavat palvelut: • johtajan soveltuvuusarviointi • esihenkilön/päällikön soveltuvuusarviointi • asiantuntijan soveltuvuusarviointi • johtajan, esihenkilön/päällikön ja asiantuntijan potentiaaliarviointi ******************************************************** Soveltuvuusarviointeja hankitaan vuodessa arviolta 40-80 kpl. Potentiaaliarviointeja tilataan Sopimuskaudella tarpeen mukaan (harvoin). Hankinnan kohdetta on kuvattu tarkemmin tarjouspyynnön liitteellä 1 (Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus). Hankintaan valitaan toteuttajaksi yksi (1) Toimittaja. Tarjoajan tulee nimetä tarjouksessaan kolme (3) Palvelua suorittavaa Asiantuntijaa. ****************************************** SOPIMUSKAUSI Varsinainen sopimuskausi on 24 kuukautta, jonka jälkeen Sopimusta voidaan jatkaa optiokaudelle 24 kk. Sopimuskauden suunniteltu alkamisajankohta on tammikuu - helmikuu 2027. HANKINNAN KOKONAISARVO Hankinnan arvioitu arvo on 80 000 euroa/ vuosi (alv 0 %). Hankinnan arvioitu kokonaisarvo on noin 320 000 euroa (alv 0 %) mukaan lukien mahdollinen optiokausi.

title: CA18634 - RFQ 2026/46 - NMANDD PEACEPLUS "Thriving Together" - Celebrating Cultures and Diversity - 3.2 Creative Language Exchange
description: Competent and creative suppliers are hereby invited to tender for the design, development, and delivery of an engaging Creative language exchange programme. The project will deliver an inclusive Creative Language Exchange programme that uses music and cultural sharing to bring people together. Participants will learn songs in different languages, explore diverse cultures, and share their own experiences in a welcoming environment. Working towards a public performance, the programme will celebrate linguistic and cultural diversity while promoting inclusion, intercultural understanding, and belonging. The programme aims to strengthen community connections, support the integration of minority communities, and build more inclusive and cohesive communities across the district. To access this competition: Registered: Login to https://suppliers.multiquote.com and view the opportunity CA18634. Not registered: Visit https://suppliers.multiquote.com then register and quote CA18634 as the reason for registration. Any queries please contact MultiQuote on 020 3920 8054.

title: 2026 - Aberdeen City - Integrated Children with Disabilities Services
description: Aberdeen City Council requires the provision of an integrated specialist support service for disabled children and young people aged from birth to 18 years who have complex and/or significant care and support needs requiring a level of specialist support beyond that ordinarily available through universal, community-based or mainstream care provision. This may include children and young people with complex health, physical, learning, developmental, sensory, communication and/or behavioural support needs, including needs associated with autism. Eligibility for, and the nature of, support will be determined by individual assessment of need, intended outcomes and the Service Provider's ability to meet those needs safely and appropriately. Short-break overnights and residential care will in the main be utilised for our older children (often teenagers.)

title: Subcontractors and Specialist Contractors for Building Services - UPVC Windows and Doors

Contractors will be required to provide details on how their organisation in terms of skill, qualifications and competence that fit and meet with the specification the skills. They will need to demonstrate they have a Waste Management plan, Contractors will also be required to provide evidence of insurance policies, where required to provide evidence of security Industry Authority Approved Contractor’s Scheme (SIA). The framework will operate on a ranked basis. title: AI-Enabled Support
description: The 48th Contracting Squadron (48 CONS) at RAF Lakenheath, on behalf of the 100th Maintenance Group (100 MXG) and the 100th Logistics Readiness Squadron (100 LRS) at RAF Mildenhall, United Kingdom, is conducting market research to identify commercial vendors capable of delivering an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-enabled maintenance decision-support and edge computing software platform. The Government requires an enterprise-capable, commercial software platform designed to ingest and modularize complex technical data�including aircraft Technical Orders (TOs), commercial and military vehicle maintenance manuals, historical maintenance records, and real-time vehicle telematics / Controller Area Network (CANbus) data. The objective is to guide maintenance technicians through step-by-step troubleshooting, diagnostic isolation, and repair workflows on ruggedized mobile edge devices in both connected and disconnected operational environments. 48 CONS is seeking information about what commercially available or production-ready solutions currently exist across industry, and is interested in understanding the technological capabilities, commercial licensing models, deployment timelines, and cybersecurity maturity (e.g., Risk Management Framework / Authority to Operate pathways) that industry can offer. This announcement constitutes an RFI for informational and planning purposes only. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), nor is it to be construed as a commitment by the Government. No contract will be awarded as a result. Industry�s response to the RFI?�or lack thereof�will have no impact on the evaluation of responses to any subsequent RFP or Request for Quote (RFQ) released. The information requested will be used within 48 CONS as market research to facilitate decision making (e.g., determining acquisition strategy, small business concerns) and will not be disclosed outside the Government. Proprietary information submitted shall be appropriately marked. Do not submit confidential information in your response. **Note** 48 CONS/ will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by interested parties responding to this RFI.

title: Cedar Shingle Roof Replacement, Ardgowan National Historic Site.
description: 5P468-26-0294/A Cedar Shingle Roof Replacement, Ardgowan National Historic Site. BIDS RECEIVED BY FAX AND EMAIL WILL BE ACCEPTED AS OFFICIAL. PARKS CANADA IS NOT CURRENTLY ACCEPTING BIDS VIA SAP ARIBA, YOU MUST SUBMIT YOUR BID VIA FAX OR EMAIL AS INDICATED IN THE SOLICITATION DOCUMENT. BIDS RECEIVED IN-PERSON OR BY COURIER WILL NOT BE ACCEPTED. The only acceptable email address for responses to the bid solicitation issoumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca . Bids submitted by email directly to the Contracting Authority or to any email address other than soumissionsami-bidsrpc@pc.gc.ca will not be accepted. The only acceptable facsimile for responses to bid solicitations is 1-855-983-1808. The maximum email file size that Parks Canada is capable of receiving is 15 megabytes. The Bidder is responsible for any failure attributable to the transmission or receipt of the emailed bid due to file size. The Bidder should be cognisant of the size of the email as a whole, and not only the attachments. Please take into consideration that some attachments, when sent, may be resized during the email transfer. If the email size is too large, the Bidder should send the bid in multiple emails properly labeled with the solicitation number, project name, and indicate how many emails are included (ex. 1 of 2). Emails with links to bid documents will not be accepted. Bid documents must be sent as email attachments. REQUIREMENT The work encompasses cedar shingle replacement, flashing replacement and integration, ventilation upgrades, and exterior wood conservation at three (3) subject roof areas TWO-SUBMISSION BID This Bid shall be submitted following a “two-submission” procedure. Refer to SI04 of the Special Instructions to Bidders. CONTRACTOR SELECTION AND INDIGENOUS PARTICIPATION PLAN The Contractor should ensure provision of specific and agreed upon benefits for Indigenous People and Indigenous Businesses in the Area of the Contract. This Invitation to Tender contains bid criteria in order to provide socioeconomic benefits to Indigenous communities within the area covered by the contract. PERIOD OF CONTRACT / DELIVERY DATE Contractor must perform and complete the Work no later than March 31, 2027. OPTIONAL SITE VISIT Arrangements have been made for the site visit to be held at 2 Palmers Lane, Charlottetown, PE C1A 5V8. on November 24, 2026. The site visit will begin at 10:00 AM AST. Bidders must communicate with the Contracting Authority no later than November 23 at 4:00 PM to confirm attendance and provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend. Bidders who do not confirm attendance provide the name(s) of the person(s) who will attend will not be allowed access to the site. Bidders will be requested to sign an attendance sheet. No alternative appointment will be given to bidders who do not attend or do not send a representative. Bidders who do not participate in the visit will not be precluded from submitting a bid. Any clarifications or changes to the bid solicitation resulting from the site visit will be included as an amendment to the bid solicitation. ENQUIRIES All enquiries of a technical and contractual nature are to be submitted to the Contracting Authority. Enquiries regarding this solicitation must be submitted in writing and should be received no later than five (5) Business days prior to the date set for solicitation closing to allow sufficient time to provide a response. Enquiries received after that time may result in an answer NOT being provided. INFORMATION National Parks Regulations require that all work is to be performed in accordance with the ordinances, laws, rules and regulations set out in the National Park Act. Bidders that consider themselves qualified to provide this Work and intend to submit bids on this project should obtain documents from the Government Electronic Tendering Service through the Government of Canada tendering service at http://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities. Addenda, when issued, will be available from the Government of Canada tendering service. Bidders that elect to base their bids on documents obtained from other sources do so at their own risk. Late submissions will not be considered. The Crown retains the right to negotiate with suppliers on any procurement. Documents may be submitted in either official language of Canada. Parks Canada has made every effort to provide equivalent documents in both official languages, however, if you find any discrepancies between the English and French documents, please notify the contract officer listed in this opportunity as soon as possible so that we can rectify the situation.

title: 2nd re-tender for fasteners and rail pads for the sleeper types: S99, SB16 & S16 for use in the Danish rail network
description: In accordance with the provisions of Directive 2014/25/EU (the Utilities Directive as implemented by Executive Order no. 1078 of 29 June 2022 on procurement by entities operating in the water, energy, transport and postal services sectors), a framework agreement for supply of fasteners and rail pads for the sleeper types: S99/SB89 and S16/SB16 for use in the Danish rail network as well as the product type acceptance process for the offered sleepers and rail pads is put out to tender. The execution of the Framework Agreement is divided into three phases: (1) Design, Validation and Product Type Acceptance Phase (2) Retrofitting of Sleeper Factory Phase (3) Manufacturing and Delivery Production Phase. The framework agreement gives Banedanmark a right, but not an obligation, to order the above-mentioned fasteners and rail pads. The Framework Agreement is exclusive regarding supply of fasteners to be used at Banedanmark's Sleeper Factory. Fasteners to be used in connection with maintenance and replacement of existing fasteners in Banedanmark’s infrastructure are not covered by this agreement. For more information reference is made to the tender material.

title: Pohjanmaan Pelastuslaitoksen nostureiden perusteelliset määräaikaistarkastukset (10-vuotistarkastus) - Grundlig periodisk inspektion (10-årskontroll) av Österbottens Räddningsverks kranar
description: Nostolaitteille pitää Valtioneuvoston asetuksen 403/2008 § 35 mukaan tehdä perusteellinen määräaikaistarkastus kerran 10:ssä vuodessa. Pohjanmaan hyvinvointialue pyytää tarjousta yhteensä kuuden (6 kpl) Pohjanmaan pelastuslaitoksen nosturin perusteellisesta määräaikaistarkastuksesta. Optiona pyydetään myös tuntihinta mahdollisille korjaustöille. Tarkastuksen kohteena olevat nosturit ovat seuraavat: 1. Palfinger PC 2300 A, vuosimalli 2005 2. Ferrari F 560 A2, vuosimalli 2005 3. Effer 2500 A2, vuosimalli 1987 4. Palfinger PC 1500 A, vuosimalli 2016 5. Hiab 650 AW, vuosimalli 1989 6. Hiab-Foco Hiab 007, vuosimalli 1996 Lisätietoa nostureiden sijoituspaikoista liitteestä 1. Hankinnan tavoitteena on valita yksi palveluntuottaja tekemään kaikki kuuden nosturin määräaikaistarkastukset. Tavoitteena on, että nostureiden tarkastukset suoritetaan talvikauden aikana siten, että ne ovat käyttökunnossa keväällä, kun veneet lasketaan takaisin vesille. Tilaajan katselmus järjestetään korjaamolla laitteen purkamisen jälkeen. Katselmuksessa sovitaan mahdollisista lisätöistä sekä purettaessa esiin tulleiden ongelmien korjaamisesta.

title: Denmark – Sleepers and parts of sleepers – 2nd re-tender for fasteners and rail pads for the sleeper types: S99, SB16 & S16 for use in the Danish rail network
description: In accordance with the provisions of Directive 2014/25/EU (the Utilities Directive as implemented by Executive Order no. 1078 of 29 June 2022 on procurement by entities operating in the water, energy, transport and postal services sectors), a framework agreement for supply of fasteners and rail pads for the sleeper types: S99/SB89 and S16/SB16 for use in the Danish rail network as well as the product type acceptance process for the offered sleepers and rail pads is put out to tender. The execution of the Framework Agreement is divided into three phases: (1) Design, Validation and Product Type Acceptance Phase (2) Retrofitting of Sleeper Factory Phase (3) Manufacturing and Delivery Production Phase. The framework agreement gives Banedanmark a right, but not an obligation, to order the above-mentioned fasteners and rail pads. The Framework Agreement is exclusive regarding supply of fasteners to be used at Banedanmark's Sleeper Factory. Fasteners to be used in connection with maintenance and replacement of existing fasteners in Banedanmark’s infrastructure are not covered by this agreement. For more information reference is made to the tender material.

title: 25-58288 Free Running Submarine Model (FRSM)
description: Free Running Submarine Model (FRSM) The National Research Council of Canada’s Ocean, Coastal and River Engineering Research Centre (NRC-OCRE) has a requirement for one (1) Free Running Submarine Model (FRSM) for delivery to St. John’s, Newfoundland and Labrador. The FRSM will support NRC’s submarine hydrodynamics research for current and future submarine designs, enabling comprehensive testing in controlled and free-running environments. NRC encourages innovative solutions and does not prescribe a specific vehicle architecture. Offerors are expected to propose an integrated design that satisfies the operational, performance, and research objectives described in this Statement of Requirement. Background NRC’s Ocean, Coastal and River Engineering Research Centre (NRC-OCRE) conducts research in submarine hydrodynamics, vehicle dynamics, control systems, and operational safety using physical and numerical modelling techniques. Over the past two decades, NRC has developed and tested several scaled submarine models, including the “Albert” model, a free-running Victoria Class submarine research platform used to investigate hydrodynamic performance, handling characteristics, seakeeping behaviour, near-bottom operations, and related submarine operating scenarios. The Albert model and associated research programs generated extensive technical data, including hydrodynamic coefficients, vehicle response characteristics, instrumentation approaches, and operational experience with free-running submarine models. Technical reference data associated with the Albert model, including geometry and historical test data, will be made available to the successful Contractor. Traditional captive models provide valuable hydrodynamic data but are limited to predefined motions and controlled test conditions. NRC requires a Free Running Submarine Model (FRSM) to expand its research capabilities through autonomous and free-running operations. The FRSM will support hydrodynamic, propulsion, autonomy, control systems, and under-ice research while providing a flexible platform that can be adapted to evaluate current and future submarine designs. The primary research objectives of the FRSM are to: 1. Generate hydrodynamic coefficients and equations of motion for different submarine configurations and operating conditions. 2. Investigate and validate the operating characteristics of current and future submarine designs. 3. Evaluate failure modes, fault responses, and emergency operating scenarios. 4. Assess vehicle control, autonomy, navigation, and mission execution strategies. 5. Support research into under-ice operations, ice interaction, and surfacing-through-ice dynamics. The FRSM must be delivered with a 1:10 scale hull geometry based on the NRC-provided Albert model, representing a simplified Victoria Class submarine configuration. The platform must also support future reconfiguration to alternative submarine geometries. To support these objectives, the FRSM must provide the following core operational capabilities: Capability Purpose Free-running autonomous submarine operations Conduct manoeuvring and mission testing without captive restraints Reconfigurable submarine research platform Evaluate current and future submarine geometries Hydrodynamic and propulsion data collection Generate hydrodynamic performance data Autonomous navigation and mission execution Support autonomy, control, and mission-planning research Under-ice operation and surfacing Support ice-interaction and Arctic research Please see tender documents for details

title: High-Altitude Platform System (HAPS) for Ultra-Long-Range (ULR) Wireless Backhaul
description: ***AMENDMENT 001 - An attachment has been added. The document contains questions and answers related to the Challenge.*** This Challenge Notice is issued under the Innovative Solutions Canada Program (ISC) Call for Proposals 004 (EN578-24ISC4). For general ISC information, Offerors can visit the ISC website at: https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en Please refer to the Solicitation Documents Innovative Solutions Canada Program Call for Proposals – 004 - Tender Notice | CanadaBuys https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 which contains the process for submitting a proposal. Steps to apply: Step 1: Read this challenge. Step 2: Read the Call for Proposals : https://canadabuys.canada.ca/en/tender-opportunities/tender-notice/cb-331-17030872 Step 3: Propose your solution here : https://ised-isde.canada.ca/site/innovative-solutions-canada/en/high-altitude-platform-system-ultra-long-range-wireless-backhaul The Department of National Defence (DND), Shared Services Canada (SSC) and National Research Council of Canada (NRC) are seeking the development of a solution that will extend the reach of ultra-long-range wireless backhaul (i.e. over-the-horizon ranges) using High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS). Challenge sponsor: National Research Council (NRC) Funding mechanism: Contract Opening date : October 20, 2026 Closing date : December 1, 2026, 14:00 Eastern time Problem statement The Government of Canada recognizes the critical role that advanced communication technologies play in supporting national defence, public safety, and the security of Canadians. Reliable and resilient connectivity in dangerous, remote, and sparsely populated regions is essential for effective defence operations, emergency response, and border monitoring. However, delivering such connectivity remains a significant challenge due to Canada’s vast geography, low population densities, and extreme environmental conditions. The Department of National Defence, Shared Services Canada and National Research Council of Canada are seeking the development of a solution that leverages High Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) to provide ultra-long-range wireless backhaul (i.e., over-the-horizon ranges). This capability will enhance communications under harsh weather or challenging terrain in theatres of conflict, in remote areas, and isolated regions with little to no current connectivity. The ultimate goal is to improve secure, high-speed communications for Canadian defence, surveillance, and emergency operations while also potentially benefiting civilian emergency response connectivity needs. The successful applicant is responsible for securing a demonstration site as well as a Special Flight Operations Certificate (SFOC) clearance from Transport Canada to demonstrate the HAPS capabilities. Desired outcomes and considerations Essential (mandatory) outcomes The proposed solution must: 1. Demonstrate the capability to travel from the surface up to 20 kilometers +/- 2 kilometers and travel laterally within the corridor of 20 kilometers +/- 2 kilometers. 2. Operate at a specified, nominal, fixed point relative to the Earth for an extended period (minimum of 3 days). 3. Launch, deploy, and operate from land or water-based environments. 4. Provide a minimum of 100 Watts to support the deployment of long-range sensors. 5. Deliver high-bandwidth, high-availability, ultra-low latency wireless connectivity comparable to current offerings (e.g. 4G/LTE, Starlink, or equivalent) in the telecommunications industry. 6. Support current (e.g. 4G/LTE, Starlink, or equivalent) wireless systems and infrastructure. 7. Provide a minimum of 1000 km² service area coverage and a minimum of 200 km² of transit area coverage based on usage demands. 8. Be deployable within 6 hours for heavier-than-air HAPS or within 24 hours for lighter-than-air HAPS. 9. Incorporate automated decision-making for flight maneuvers and operations. 10. Operate at cold temperatures between -50 to at least -70 degrees Celsius. Additional outcomes The proposed solution should: 1. Have a power management system that optimizes power consumption and adapts to usage demand. 2. Be capable of continuous power generation and recharging during ground operations and flight through renewable energy sources. 3. Have non-assisted launch and land capability from land or water-based environments. 4. Support next generation wireless systems and infrastructure. 5. Maintain wireless connectivity in the presence of intentional and unintentional wireless channel interference. 6. Provide communications link security features and platform hardening to prevent signal interception, hacking and unauthorized platform hijacking. 7. Demonstrate the ability to daisy chain the signal using intra-HAPS (i.e HAPS group 1 to HAPS group2), and/or inter-HAPS (between individual HAPS). 8. Support backhauling requirements for future wireless networks. 9. Complement the terrestrial communication infrastructures. 10. Minimize the amount of traditional backhaul hopping. 11. Support point-to-point, point-to-multipoint, and mesh links. Background and context High-Altitude Platform Systems (HAPS) are unmanned vehicles designed to operate in the stratosphere at altitudes of 20 to 50 kilometers above the Earth's surface. HAPS are classified into two main types: Lighter-than-air (LTA) platforms and Heavier-than-air (HTA) platforms. LTA platforms include balloons and airships characterized by low energy consumption but has limited maneuverability. On the other hand, HTA platforms which include light unmanned aircrafts that rely on electric motors to generate and maintain lift offer greater maneuverability but have payload weight restrictions and can have an energy deficit issue as a result of prolonged dark periods during winter months at higher latitudes. HAPS offer several advantages such as its ability to be airborne for long durations and less expensive to operate compared to satellites. Since HAPS fly at lower altitudes than satellites, they are able to provide low latency data communications. The propulsion systems for HAPS generally use sustainable energy sources which have a lower environmental impact than rocket launches for satellites. Presently, existing wireless backhaul technologies have limitations in terms of coverage and during emergency situations for remote areas, nomadic users, and scattered populations. A merging solution between HAPS and ULR (Ultra-Long-Range) wireless backhaul, offering broadband services, would be a great benefit to a wide range of populations, especially in times of crisis and during emergency situations where traditional telecommunication services suffer outages. Additionally, HAPS are highly effective platforms for enhancing military communications and remote sensing capabilities. They can be used to complement military satcom infrastructure, offering capabilities in intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) missions. When equipped with high-resolution cameras, radars, and signals intelligence systems (SIGINT), HAPS provide continuous coverage of areas of interest. title: Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2
description: NOTICE OF PROPOSED PROCUREMENT Canada has a requirement for the items detailed below: GSIN: N1375 – Demolition Materials UNSPSC: 46101600 –Ammunition Description: Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 A requirement exists to resupply Canada with the Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2. The Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 is required as a specialized explosive charge used by combat engineers to breach barbed wire obstacles/entanglements and to clear a path through anti-personnel mines, without requiring personnel to approach the obstacle directly under fire. The system consists of several cylindrical sections of tubes/pipes that can be connected end-to end to create a linear explosive charge of desired length. A blunt, rounded nose sleeve is attached to the leading end of the assembly, allowing the torpedo to be pushed or shoved through obstacles, such as concertina wire or across rough terrain, without snagging. The Demolition Kit, Bangalore Torpedo M1A2 is primed with a blasting cap. When detonated, the pipe itself contributes to the effect: the metal casing fractures into high-velocity fragments that shred the surrounding wire, while the explosive blast clears a path for infantry to advance. description: Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (myöhemmin myös Tilaaja) pyytää osallistumishakemuksia kotiin vietävien palvelujen hankintaa varten. Kyseessä on julkisista hankinnoista ja käyttöoikeuksista annetun lain 1397/2016 (hankintalain) liitteen E mukainen hankinta. Hankinta toteutetaan dynaamisena toimittajarekisterinä, joka tarkoittaa hankintayksikön itsensä suunnittelemaa, hankintalain periaatteiden mukaista menettelyä hankinnan kohteena olevien palveluiden hankkimiseen. Hankinnan kohteena on Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueen omia kotiin vietäviä palveluja täydentävä ostopalvelu. Tarkempi kuvaus hankinnan sisällöstä on osallistumispyynnön liitteellä 2 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue valitsee dynaamiseen toimittajarekisteriin kaikki Palveluntuottajat, jotka täyttävät tällä osallistumispyynnöllä ja tämän osallistumispyynnön liitteillä asetetut vaatimukset. Sopimuskausi on toistaiseksi voimassa oleva. Tällä osallistumispyynnöllä otsikoissa esiintyvä käsite "tarjouspyyntö" viittaa tähän osallistumispyyntöön. Tällä osallistumispyynnöllä otsikoissa esiintyvä käsite "tarjous" viittaa osallistumishakemukseen., Kotiin vietävät palvelut osakohteet 1-6 Osa-alueen tarkempi kuvaus liitteellä 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus"., Kotiin vietävät palvelut osakohde 7 Karkkila, Siuntio, Hanko, Inkoo Osa-alueen tarkempi kuvaus liitteellä 1 "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus".,

title: Kouvolan kaupungin pienet purkutyöt v.2027
description: Kouvolan kaupungin pienet purkutyöt v.2027 Kouvolan kaupunki hakee puitesopimuskumppaneita kaupungin pienille purkutöille vuodelle 2027. Toimeksiannot ovat Kouvolan kaupungin pienien rakennusten purkutöitä. Purkutyön toimeksianto voi sisältää myös alihankintaa, esim. asbestipurkutyöt. Toimeksiantojen kohteet sijaitsevat Kouvolan alueella. Tyypillisimpiä kohteita ovat puurakenteiset omakotitalot perustuksineen. Purkutoimeksiantoon tavallisesti kuuluu rakennukseen liittyvien LVIS-tele-järjestelmien purkaminen kiinteistöstä, kaivaminen ja tulppaaminen tilaajan esittämiin kohtiin sekä purkualueen tasaus. Puitesopimuksessa sekä toimeksiannossa noudetaan YSE 1998 sopimusehtoja ellei tarjouspyynnössä tai sopimuksessa toisin mainittu. Puitesopimusjärjestelyyn pääsevät mukaan kaikki tarjouspyynnön soveltuvuusvaatimukset, kelpoisuusehdot ja hankinnan kohteen kriteerit täyttävät tarjoajat. Sopimuskautena ei sitouduta mihinkään hankintamääriin. Toimeksiantojen antaminen liitteenä olevan sopimusluonnoksen mukaisesti. Ennen työn aloittamista urakoitsija antaa kirjallisen arvion kohteen urakkakustannuksista. Työn toteuttamisen ajankohta ja valmistuminen sovitaan ennen työn aloittamista. Lähtökohtaisesti tämän kilpailutuksen puitesopimuksia käyttää Kouvolan Tilapalvelut sekä Tekniikan ja ympäristön toimiala, mutta myös muut kaupungin yksiköt voivat hyödyntää puitesopimuksia. Lisäksi puitejärjestelyyn kuuluu osallistuminen purkutyöhön liittyvään kehitystyöhön. Tilaajan tavoitteena on kehittää purkutyön tilausta ja suoritusta tukemaan enemmän kiertotalouden tavoitteiden saavuttamista. Kehitystyön sisällöstä ja kustannuksista sovitaan erikseen toimeksiantokohtaisesti ja ne voivat sisältyä yksittäiseen purkutyön toimeksiantoon.,

title: FCI Leavenworth Cable Television Services
description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons, Federal Correctional Institution Leavenworth, requests quotations for cable television services from eligible vendors. Quotation Requirements: Vendors shall submit: � A proposed channel lineup identifying how it meets the SOW requirements and clearly identifying any substitutions or exceptions. � A brief technical approach explaining how service will be provided to approximately 115 television drops at the FCI and FPC using the existing distribution system. Identify any equipment, installation, or modifications required and describe responsibility for equipment maintenance and repairs. � A transition approach identifying the time required to activate service and measures to minimize service interruptions. � A description of telephone support, outage assessment, on-site response, and service restoration capabilities. � References for up to three recent, relevant contracts involving comparable television distribution services. Vendors without relevant past performance shall state that in their quotation. � Separate pricing for the base period and each of the four option periods, including recurring service, installation, equipment, preventive maintenance, and any other charges necessary to perform the SOW. Identify any exceptions to the requested terms. Comparative Evaluation: The Government will use a comparative evaluation to determine which quotation provides the best value. Quotations will be compared directly against one another using technical capability, past performance, and price. Numerical scores will not be assigned. Technical capability will consider the proposed channel lineup, compatibility with the existing distribution system, installation and transition approach, and ability to meet maintenance and outage-response requirements. Past performance will consider available information regarding successful performance of similar services, including reliability, responsiveness, and customer satisfaction. A vendor without relevant past performance will receive a neutral assessment under this factor. Technical capability and past performance, when combined, are more important than price. The Government may select a higher-priced quotation when its documented benefits justify the additional price. Total evaluated price will include the base period, all four option periods, and all required charges. Evaluation of options does not obligate the Government to exercise them. Select Best-Suited, Then Negotiate: The Government intends to select the best-suited vendor based on the initial quotations but reserves the right to conduct exchanges. After identifying the apparent best-suited vendor, the Government may negotiate price, technical details, transition arrangements, or other terms with that vendor to finalize the requirement and obtain the best value. title: DE01--Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) Managed Services (VA-27-00019920)
description: IT Enterprise Service Desk (ESD) Managed Services Request for Information VA-27-00019920 Introduction This Request for Information (RFI) is for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products or services described in this RFI. Your response to this RFI will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI. This request does not constitute a solicitation for proposals or the authority to enter into negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541512 with a size standard of $34 million. VA seeks market research on industry capability to meet the draft Performance Work Statement (PWS), the feasibility of key requirements, barriers to competition, and recommended changes. Responses should address the specific PWS requirements rather than provide generic marketing or capability statements. Cite relevant PWS paragraph numbers and clearly mark proprietary information. For each numbered question, indicate whether the principal requirements are (a) achievable as written, (b) achievable with modifications, or (c) not currently achievable; explain material limitations and recommend specific changes. Respondents may propose functionally equivalent, technology-neutral solutions. Responses shall be limited to 20 pages, excluding the cover/firm information, comparable-experience summary, and ROM attachment. Respondents shall indicate its company name and address; point of contact, phone, and email; business size and socioeconomic status; applicable NAICS code(s); Unique Entity Identifier (UEI); and available contract vehicles (GWAC, FSS, or MAC). VOSB/SDVOSB respondents should provide proof of SBA certification. Separately provide a concise summary of comparable contracts (agency, contract number, approximate value, and reference contact, if available). Additionally, VOSB/SDVOSB respondents shall indicate your company s intent and ability to meet the set aside requirement in accordance with VAAR 852.219-73 (JAN 2023) (DEVIATION) VA Notice of Total Set-Aside For Certified SDVOSBs and 13 CFR §125.6, which states the contractor will not pay more than 50% of the amount paid by the government to the prime for contract performance to firms that are not certified SDVOSBs listed in the SBA certification database (excluding direct costs to the extent they are not the principal purpose of the acquisition and the SDVOSB/VOSB does not provide the service, such as airline travel, cloud computing services, or mass media purchases). When a contract includes both services and supplies, the 50 percent limitation shall apply only to the service portion of the contract. Your response shall include information as to available personnel and financial resources; full names of proposed team members and the PWS requirements planned to be subcontracted to them, which must include the prime planned percentage or the names of the potential team members that may be used to fulfill the set aside requirement. Your response must address capabilities specific to the services required in the attached PWS and must address the following: 1. Transition-In and Service Continuity (PWS 5.2 and 5.4.6) The draft PWS provides two concurrent transition tracks: Track A for platform/CCI services (approximately Day 60 operational transfer when retaining the current platform or Day 150 for a different platform) and Track B for Tier 0/Tier 1 services (100% workload at required service levels within 150 calendar days), with Quality Gates and 30 days of hypercare after each transfer. Can your company meet these timelines while maintaining uninterrupted functionality and customer experience? Identify the most consequential dependencies, transition risks, baseline verification and operational transfer readiness criteria, and any alternative sequencing or technology approaches that would reduce risk. How should VA address capabilities discovered after award that are absent from the Functional Baseline (Attachment 2)? Identify only authorization, integration, or other deliverable deadlines that materially affect feasibility. 2. Managed Services Delivery Model and Tier 0/Tier 1 Operations (PWS 3.0, 4.2, 5.3, 5.4, 5.5.5, and 5.6) Can your company deliver the integrated Tier 0/Tier 1 service desk, CCI, knowledge management, process integration, quality assurance, and performance reporting requirements through a single managed service, with results independently verified for VA? Identify capability gaps, specialized teaming needs, or requirements that could unnecessarily restrict competition. Comment on feasibility of the draft workload assumptions, including approximately 2,700 knowledge articles (15% annual growth), 520 instructional videos annually, approximately 35 concurrent process-integration initiatives (10% annual growth), Top 10 user support, and Enterprise Command Center support via Tier 1 Incident Management Analysts. What changes or technology-neutral approaches would improve delivery without reducing required outcomes? 3. Artificial Intelligence and Automation Capabilities (PWS 5.8) Can your company implement and operate the AI and automation capabilities described in the PWS, including conversational, generative and agentic AI, robotic process automation, self-service, agent-assist knowledge surfacing, and post-interaction summaries? Distinguish commercially available capabilities from those requiring configuration, integration, or custom development; identify security, data, quality assurance, and operational dependencies. Describe how inaccurate AI-generated content would be detected and corrected before entry into permanent records. Recommend additional capabilities that could materially improve resolution, accessibility, customer experience, or agent productivity, distinguishing demonstrated solutions from emerging functionality. 4. Automation Glide Path Feasibility and Governance (PWS 5.8.3 5.8.5, 5.8.10, 5.8.11, 5.8.14, and 6.1.12) The draft PWS proposes human-handled capacity of 92%, 82%, 72%, 65%, and 60% of a certified baseline in Years 1 5 (50% floor), using approximately 126,000 monthly contacts as the current planning baseline. Are these targets achievable while sustaining service quality? Recommend changes to baseline certification, timing, assumptions, exclusions, and measurement, including the definition of an Automated Resolution (no agent and no repeat contact within seven days), treatment of pre-existing automation, and human-handled contacts per 1,000 End Users. Address how AI-attempted contacts escalated to agents should be counted and reported. Are the proposed approval controls practical (intent-level parity baseline of approximately 90 days, Automation Deployment Package, approximately 15-business-day VA review, and rollback within approximately 15 minutes for voice/chat or four hours for other channels)? Recommend changes that balance deployment speed, auditability, accessible escalation, and protection against unsuccessful deflection. Include any potential price and service level impacts associated with the glide path iterative drops in human-handled capacity. 5. Staffing, Workforce Management, and Surge Capacity (PWS 4.2, 5.1.4, 5.3, and 5.8.7) Can your company meet 24/7/365 support from continental U.S. facilities, the required service levels, and the proposed peak-day planning assumption

The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, transportation, tools, access equipment, routine maintenance materials, cleaning supplies, waste handling, testing, service labels, and documentation required by this PWS. The recurring scope includes five kitchen fire suppression systems and five Kidde IND-21 Hazmat dry chemical systems, with monthly inspections of all ten systems, semiannual maintenance and service certification, and annual maintenance tasks. All five hoods require quarterly exhaust inspections and complete interior and exterior cleaning. The Building 402 grease trap requires quarterly inspection, pump-out, and cleaning. Appendix A identifies equipment and locations; Appendix B states service quantities, deliverables, and performance standards. The prime Contractor remains responsible for all subcontracted work and for submitting complete records directly to the COR. A kitchen cleaning report does not document fire suppression system maintenance, monthly suppression inspections, or grease-trap service; each service shall have its own identifiable record.

C.2 EPO 18-01 EPO SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT FEE AND SUBMISSION OF QUARTERLY SALES REPORTS: OPEN MARKET (JAN 2016) a. Service Level Agreement Fee. The Service Level Agreement (SLA) fee is established by the Supply Fund Board and is provided as a means of reimbursement for customary acquisition-related services necessary to obtain contractor services and/or supplies as required. The SLA is reimbursed to the EPO based on rates established by the supply fund board and are recouped based on a percentage of total quarterly sales. The Supply Fund Board may change the percentage at any time, but typically not more than once per year. Upon a change in the SLA, the Contracting Officer (CO) shall issue a unilateral modification to apply the change to CLIN prices based upon the SLA rate change. The EPO will provide reasonable notice prior to the effective date of the change. In order to facilitate SLA reimbursement, offerors must include (imbed) the SLA fee into their prices; therefore, the fee will be reflected in the total amount charged and transparent to ordering activities. The current SLA which applies to this contract action is 0.5%. This SLA Fee shall be imbedded in the awarded contract/agreement price(s) and offers submitted in response to this solicitation shall include this SLA Fee in the price of every line item offered. b. Quarterly Sales Reports. The Contractor must report all contract sales under this contract and submit collected SLAs as follows: (1) The Contractor must accurately report the dollar value, in U.S. dollars and rounded to the nearest whole dollar, of all sales made under this contract by calendar quarter (January 1 March 31, April 1 June 30, July 1 September 30, and October 1 December 31). Reported sales must include all sales made to all authorized contract or agreement users, whether shipped directly to the users or through Prime Vendor contractors. The report must reflect sales by contract line item and segment sales by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) and Other Government Agencies (OGA). The reported contract sales must include the SLA Fee and each quarterly report must show the total SLA Fee amount collected on the reported sales. The Contractor must maintain a consistent accounting method of sales reporting, based on the Contractor s established commercial accounting practice. The Contractor must consistently use only one of the following acceptable points at which sales may be reported- i. Receipt of order; ii. Shipment or delivery, as applicable; iii. Issuance of an invoice; or iv. Payment. (2) Sales under this contract/agreement shall be reported to the EPO within 60 calendar days following the completion of each reporting quarter. The Contractor must continue to furnish quarterly reports, including zero sales, through physical completion of the last outstanding order of the contract/agreement. (3) The sales report signed by an authorized representative of the contractor shall be emailed to the appropriate individual(s) listed in the terms and conditions of the contract or agreement. c. SLA Remittance The Contractor must remit the SLA fee to the EPO in U.S. dollars within 60 calendar days after the end of the reporting quarter and final payment shall be remitted within 60 days after physical completion of the last outstanding task order or delivery order of the contract. The SLA Fee amount collected and due shall be paid electronically. To ensure that the payment is credited properly, the Contractor must electronically transmit the SLA fee along with the coinciding quarterly sales report at www.pay.gov (VA Enterprise Procurement Office (EPO)); specific instructions must be provided when the contract action resulting from this solicitation is awarded (i.e. post-award/BPA issuance conference and/or post-award letter when used in lieu of a conference). The Government reserves the right to inspect, without further notice, such records of the Contractor as pertinent to sales under any contract or agreements resulting from this solicitation. Failure to remit the full amount of the SLA within 60 calendar days after the end of the applicable reporting period constitutes a contract debt to the United States Government under the terms of Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Subpart 32.6. The Government may exercise all rights under the Debt Collection Improvement Act of 1996, including withholding or setting off payments and interest on the debt (see RFO clause 52.232-17, Interest). Should the Contractor fail to submit the required sales reports, falsify them, or fail to timely pay the SLA, the Government shall have, in addition to the rights and remedies described in this clause, all other rights and remedies permitted by Federal law and statutes. (End of Clause)

NOTICE FOR FILING AGENCY PROTESTS United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) Ombudsman Program The United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) is committed to fair, transparent, and efficient acquisitions. Interested parties with concerns about this solicitation are encouraged to seek esolution through the following USDA procedures. Tier 1: Contracting Officer Concern Resolution Submission: Interested parties with concerns about either the solicitation or subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to llow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority will not consider an appeal of the Contracting Officer�s decision on an agency protest. The protest must state whether the protester elects review by the Contracting Officer, by the UDSA Independent Review Authority. If no election is stated, the Contracting Officer will decide the protest. Required Information: Protests shall include the information set forth in FAR 33.104-4 (a)(3). Failure to submit the required information may result in a delay or dismissal of the protest. Submission: Agency protests should be submitted electronically to SPE.inquiry@usda.gov and the Contracting Officer. Timeliness: Protests must be filed within the timeframes specified in FAR 33.104. Effect on Award or Performance: Contract awards or performance will be suspended during the protest period unless justified in writing for urgent and compelling reasons or determined to be in the best interest of the Government. Review Timeline: USDA strives to resolve agency-level protests within 35 business days of receipt. Election of Forum: By filing a protest with USDA, the protesters agree not to file a protest on the same matter with the Government Accountability Office (GAO) or any other external forum while the agency protest is pending. If such a protest is filed externally, the USDA agency protest will be dismissed. Questions: Questions regarding this notice or protest procedures should be directed to the Contracting Officer identified in this solicitation.

title: J012--Fire Suppression System Maintenance and
description: Fire Suppression System Maintenance and Kitchen Exhaust Cleaning Richard L Roudebush VA Medical Center 1481 West 10th Street, Indianapolis, Indiana 46202 Additional service location: 9045 East 59th Street, Building 402, Indianapolis, Indiana 46216 The Contractor shall maintain the identified fire suppression systems in a serviceable condition, remove grease accumulation from the complete identified kitchen exhaust systems, and maintain the Building 402 grease trap. The Contractor shall provide all labor, supervision, transportation, tools, access equipment, routine maintenance materials, cleaning supplies, waste handling, testing, service labels, and documentation required by this PWS. The recurring scope includes five kitchen fire suppression systems and five Kidde IND-21 Hazmat dry chemical systems, with monthly inspections of all ten systems, semiannual maintenance and service certification, and annual maintenance tasks. All five hoods require quarterly exhaust inspections and complete interior and exterior cleaning. The Building 402 grease trap requires quarterly inspection, pump-out, and cleaning. Appendix A identifies equipment and locations; Appendix B states service quantities, deliverables, and performance standards. The prime Contractor remains responsible for all subcontracted work and for submitting complete records directly to the COR. A kitchen cleaning report does not document fire suppression system maintenance, monthly suppression inspections, or grease-trap service; each service shall have its own identifiable record.

title: Weapons Effect Solicitation
description: This solicitation is related to Notice IDs: N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-0014 and N00167-25-RFP-CD-66-0014_Rev1. The contractor shall provide scientific and technical services with experts in UNDEX and AIREX analysis of undersea and surface vessels to develop and utilize specialized software codes that: 1) Aid in the selection of live fire events and provide support to live fire test and evaluation programs; 2) Simulate an underwater shock environment from a far field or near miss location; 3) Simulate the response of Navy platforms to UNDEX and AIREX for far field, near miss, contact, and internally detonating weapon attacks; 4) Check the integrity of computational models; 5) Solve finite element models elastic-plastic response and reduced order engineering tools to UNDEX and AIREX events; and 6) Simulate a nuclear underwater shock environment or nuclear air blast environment from a far field location. title: S205--FY27 Solid Waste Collection Services
description: SOLICITATION DESCRIPTION The VA Caribbean Healthcare System (VACHS), 10 Casia St, San Juan, PR 00921, has a requirement for Solid Waste Collection Services. Services will include solid waste and recyclable waste collection services at various locations of the VACHS, to include the main facility at San Juan, PR, its Carolina Warehouse, and its Mayaguez Out-patient Clinic (MOPC). Collection services include four (4) electric compactors (three at VACHS and one at MOPC), in addition to four open-top dumpsters at VACHS, and two open-top dumpsters at the Carolina Warehouse. The Contractor shall have the resources necessary for the provision these services. Waste Collection services include the collection of Recyclable Waste, which is composed of wooden pallets, aluminum, plastic, and vegetative waste. North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this requirement is 62111 (Solid Waste Collection), and the Product Service Code (PSC) is S205 (Housekeeping Trash/Garbage Collection). Government will award a contract resulting from this solicitation to the responsible Quoter whose quote conforming to the solicitation will be most advantageous to the Government, price and other factors considered. The following factors will be used to evaluate quotes: 1. Technical Capability: The technical submission will primarily determine the qualifications and capability of the quoter to participate in this contract. It should be specific and complete in every detail. The submission should be concise and provide sufficient information to demonstrate the quoter s capacity to satisfactory perform the task(s) outlined in the solicitation. Content of technical submission - The technical submission shall include at a minimum: i. A technical approach that details how the requirements of the PWS will be accomplished. ii. Sufficient documentation (including brochures, pamphlets, product literature, etc.), to allow thorough evaluation of the quote. iii. Demonstrate the ability to meet the requirements in the solicitation as stated in the PWS. iv. Vendor must also submit the following: - License to transport and dispose of Solid Waste in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, provided by the Puerto Rico Department of Natural Resources. - Permit to dispose of Solid Waste in Puerto Rico landfills. - Department of Transportation (DOT) permit for vehicles transporting Solid Waste. 2. Past Performance: The past performance submissions will primarily determine the competency of the quoter s historical performance, and how that competency can be employed to predict the quoter s success in performing the task(s) listed in the solicitation. Content of Past Performance Submittal - The past performance shall include at a minimum: i. A list of Points of Contact (POCs) for two current or previous contracts and/or agreements you have with other public or private firms for the type of work included in this solicitation. ii. This information should include name, email address, and telephone number. 3. Price: The pricing submission will primarily inform the Government as to the prices the vendor can perform the work in accordance with the solicitation. Questions submission shall be received not later than 12:00 PM Atlantic Standard Time (AST) on November 20, 2026 at wilfredo.perez3@va.gov. Submission of your response shall be received not later than 12:00 PM AST on December 1, 2026 at wilfredo.perez3@va.gov. The quoter shall submit a PDF version of the quote to the Government. Late submissions shall be treated in accordance with the solicitation provision at FAR 52.212-1(c). Omission of any one item MAY result in a quoter package being deemed not technically acceptable. description: Danės upės Klaipėdos miesto savivaldybės teritorijoje valymo, gilinimo ir tvarkymo darbų projekto parengimo paslaugų pirkimo RINKOS KONSULTACIJA. Rinkos konsultacija skelbiama iki pirkimo pradžios. Rinkos konsultacija nėra skelbimas apie pirkimą ar išankstinis skelbimas apie pirkimą. Šios rinkos konsultacijos paskelbimu dalyviai nėra kviečiami varžytis dėl pirkimo sutarties. Dalyvavimas rinkos konsultacijoje yra neatlygintinas, nesuteikiantis pirmenybinio statuso dalyvaujant pirkime. Jokios išlaidos dalyviams neatlyginamos, kompensacijos nemokamos, dalyvavimas rinkos konsultacijoje neturi įtakos ir nesuteikia dalyviui pirmenybės viešiesiems pirkimams, kurie bus skelbiami ateityje, ar jų rezultatams. Rinkos konsultacijos tikslas - informuoti tiekėjus apie planuojamą pirkimą, išsiaiškinti įvairius su pirkimo objektu susijusius klausimus, pasiruošti pirkimui įvertinant pateiktus dokumentus.

title: Conversion & Commercial Fit-Out of 90 Hermon Hill E18 to 105-Place Nursery - HW/4699
description: Happywoods Nursery is seeking an experienced commercial main contractor to undertake the full internal conversion, refurbishment, and fit-out of 90 Hermon Hill, South Woodford, London, E18 1QB, converting a vacant former care home into a 105-place children's day nursery with top-floor administrative offices. Scope & Design Specification Summary (per Dovetail Architects Design Brief Rev 0 & Drawings PL-100 to PL-122): - Classrooms (Babies, Toddlers & 3-5 Years): Forbo welded non-slip vinyl with matching cap & cove; 3mm plaster skim with Dulux Matt Emulsion; Rockfon Blanka dB35 suspended ceilings (600x600mm grid); veneered fire doors with vision panels, finger guards, closers/back-checks & kick plates; adult/child-height handleless base units, 28mm square-edge worktops (mason's mitre), 400mm WhiteRoc splashbacks & SS 1.5 bowl sinks. - WCs & Nappy Change: Forbo welded vinyl; 1200mm WhiteRoc wall panelling; 18mm HPL IPS enclosures & 1100mm cubicles; Armitage Shanks Contour 21 Splash WCs (305/355mm); Franke Wave trough sinks with Avon 21 self-closing taps; Concept Arc 55cm basins; full DDA sanitary packs. - First Floor Commercial Kitchen & Laundry: Full-height WhiteRoc wall panelling; handleless units; min. 2 sinks plus hand-rinse basin; 304 food-grade fully welded SS extraction canopy with baffle filters, LED lights & speed-controlled fan; dedicated AC heating/cooling. - Stair Cores, Offices & Staff Room: Forbo carpet tiles with 150x18mm single-groove MDF skirting; contrasting stair nosings; dual-height brushed 304 SS handrails; 10mm toughened clear glass balustrades; perimeter dado trunking at 850mm FFL; staff kitchenette with microwave housing & 400mm WhiteRoc splashback. - MEP & Security: Central boiler serving Low Surface Temperature (LST) radiators throughout, supplemented by air conditioning units in classrooms, offices & kitchen/laundry; L1 fire alarm & secure video intercom. - Acoustic & External Works (per Clear Acoustic Design Report CAD-26116): Continuous 2.0m absorptive acoustic timber boundary fencing (Jackson's Jakoustic or approved equal, min. 15 kg/m2 surface mass with sealed base junctions); acoustic sealing/lining to party wall adjoining 92 Hermon Hill; Falcon Way drop-off & external play surfacing. Contract & Site Terms: - Form of Contract: JCT Intermediate Building Contract with Contractor's Design (ICD) or JCT Minor Works with Contractor's Design. - Site Possession & DBS Exemption: The property is vacant and unoccupied; full site possession transfers to the Principal Contractor under CDM 2015. Because no children are on site during works, Enhanced DBS clearance is NOT required. Additional information: Site Access, Logistics & Key Notes for Tendering Contractors: Accompanied Site Visits: Site inspections at 90 Hermon Hill (E18 1QB) are strictly by prior appointment during the tender period. Contractors are strongly encouraged to inspect existing M&E incoming capacities, structural layouts, party-wall conditions, and external garden levels prior to submitting pricing. Traffic, Deliveries & Neighbour Amenity: The site sits at the junction of Hermon Hill and Falcon Way, directly adjoining residential properties (including 92 Hermon Hill and Osprey Close). Contractors must factor in a practical Traffic & Logistics Management Plan covering material deliveries, skip positioning, and strict adherence to London Borough of Redbridge permitted construction working hours. Design Brief & Acoustic Compliance: Tenderers must price strictly in accordance with the attached HappyWoods Design Brief (June 2026, Rev 0) and Clear Acoustic Design Noise Impact Assessment (CAD-26116)-specifically the continuous 2.0m absorptive acoustic timber fencing (minimum 15 kg/m² surface mass with sealed base junctions) and party-wall soundproofing specifications. Unoccupied Site / DBS Exemption: The building is vacant and unoccupied; full site possession will transfer to the Principal Contractor under CDM Regulations 2015. Enhanced DBS clearance is NOT required for construction operatives. Clarifications (RFIs): All technical or commercial queries during the tender period must be submitted through this portal's messaging function so anonymized responses can be issued simultaneously to all bidders.

buyer: North York Moors National Park Authority
title: Runswick Bay Public wifi design and install
description: To deliver a reliable, free and easy-to-use public Wi-Fi network for Runswick Bay that improves the visitor experience and overall connectivity, provides useful visitor data, while respecting the character of the village and the special qualities of the National Park. The following outputs are mandatory requirements for this brief: 1: A fully installed and operational network by June 2027. 2: Free, legally compliant access (Digital Economy Act 2010, content filtering, UK GDPR). 3: Remote monitoring, maintenance and support for the three-year term. 4: Visitor analytics reporting. The contract will run for three years from the date the network is fully installed and operational.

title: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services - Bismark, ND
description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION: GSA Fleet Lease Vehicle Auction & Marshalling Services 1.0 Description The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Bismark, ND area. Auction and marshalling site tasks include, but are not limited to: Advise the government on optimal disposition strategy for individual exchange/sale-eligible vehicles worldwide to maximize public participation and net proceeds, to include strategies for specialty (law enforcement, buses, ambulances, medium & heavy trucks, etc.) as well as Zero Emission Vehicles to include battery electric vehicles, plug-in hybrid vehicles and/or fuel cell vehicles. Perform full vehicle inspections and ensure complete condition reporting, imagery capture (including high-definition photo and video, 360� views, etc.), and accurate description writing. Provide recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Create and execute marketing plans/campaigns to catalog vehicles and announce vehicle sales to the public as required by law, and to advertise to/connect with the broadest possible market audience. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles and vehicle-related assets (e.g., license plates, removed equipment, telematics devices). Support the creation and management of all required vehicle disposition documentation/records. Conduct activities related to bidder/buyer management, including registration, validation/eligibility checks, etc. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to bidders/buyers throughout the sales process to ensure a seamless, transparent, and customer-centric buying experience. Facilitate and perform payment collection process. Encourage maximum participation by offering a range of non-government affiliated services (retail financing, aftermarket warranties, vehicle enhancement etc.). Store, service and remarket of electric vehicles to include any necessary charging infrastructure. Transport vehicles to and from vendor locations. Prepare vehicles for public inspection and final sales/disposition, including services such as reconditioning, maintenance and repair, as well as equipment removal/disposal, and license plate & government credit card disposal and tracking. Offer industry-aligned services for customers to perform vehicle test drives. Provide state-of-the-art technology that will improve customer experience including enhanced condition reporting, 360� views, video, high-definition photography, etc. Conduct a full and open competitive sales process, including public inspection periods for all vehicles, and any related sale services for exchange/sale property. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage, and release of vehicles from time of receipt until final removal. Manage the logistics of vehicle transportation to bring vehicles to sale. Prepare vehicles for sale, to include vehicle equipment removal/disposal, reconditioning, and repairs. Work with local government entities to facilitate any inspections, documentation, and any other actions required to complete transactions in local markets. Perform electronic inventory management, vehicle inspection, complete condition reporting for vehicles. Offer recommendations on vehicle repairs and pricing, given vehicle condition, local market environment, among any other factors, to ensure the greatest return on investment. Provide customer service to buyers in global markets. Create and execute marketing campaigns for local markets. Offer an internet sales platform with the potential to reach a global audience. Collect proceeds from vehicle sales and if necessary, convert to U.S. dollars. Marshalling only site tasks include, but are not limited to: Transport or resource/transportation of vehicles to and from vendor location (e.g., customer location, OEM dealership, offsite repair facility). Inspect vehicles upon delivery for various factors including but not limited to any damage to the vehicle, all components of the vehicle are accounted for (e.g., keys, floor mats, etc.), and missing equipment. Perform telematics device installation and/or activation on all new vehicles prior to releasing the vehicle to the customer. Validate new vehicles and options to vehicle order information provided by GSA. Perform pre-delivery inspections (PDI) in accordance with the manufacturer�s standards. Prepare new vehicles for customer receipt. Provide driver education for customers including vehicle operation, unique features, infotainment settings, etc. Offer specialized expertise and support on Electric Vehicle management, operation and charging infrastructure. Charge battery-powered vehicles. Maintain all vehicle fuel and charge levels as prescribed in the Statement of Work by GSA. Perform custodial and sales preparation services to facilitate auction house sales of GSA exchange lease vehicles. Process and manage all required vehicle shipment and delivery documentation. Manage scheduled vehicle appointments and ensure accurate vehicle exchanges. Perform all necessary tasks associated with confirming vehicle assignment and termination to and from the customer as prescribed by GSA. Provide end-to-end customer service and support to GSA Fleet and customer agencies throughout the marshalling process to ensure a seamless and transparent delivery and exchange process. Fulfill proper disposal of old/expired plates both front and back as prescribed by GSA. Perform electronic inventory management for vehicles. Ensure and facilitate the security, storage and inventory control of vehicles, license plates, credit cards and other assets from time of receipt until final removal. Scale charging capabilities to meet the needs of increasing electric vehicle adoption. Place of Performance The General Services Administration (GSA) Office of Fleet Management (GSA Fleet) has a requirement to acquire contractor support for vehicle auction and marshalling services or marshalling only services for Government vehicles. Services are required in the Bismark, ND. Interested parties must be located no more than 50 miles from the Bismark, ND area. Period of Performance On or about October 1, 2026 � September 30, 2030 (Base plus 3 option years) 2.0 Background GSA Fleet provides a full-service fleet management program providing transportation solutions to partner agencies worldwide across the U.S. Federal government. It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements. They must also be open to the general public and provide an equal opportunity for individuals, businesses, government entities, and other organizations to take part in a zero-fee, fully open, and competitive sales

description: REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI): Federal Occupational Health � Medications, Vaccines, and Medical Supplies (MVMS) The Government is issuing a Request for Information (RFI) and seeking industry feedback regarding the previous solicitations identified above. The previous solicitation (attached as Draft Solicitation) did not generate the level of industry response and/or proposal quality anticipated by the Government. Accordingly, the Government is interested in engaging with industry to better understand potential factors that may have affected vendor participation and the quality of submissions received. The Government is seeking candid feedback to identify potential improvements to the acquisition strategy and future solicitation requirements. title: STANDARD LABOR DATA COLLECTION AND SITRIBUTION APPLICATION (SLDCADA) DRAFT REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL
description: PAE Mission Systems is soliciting proposals from the eligible SeaPort-NxG small-business contract holders for end-to-end sustainment and infrastructure support of the Standard Labor Data Collection and Distribution Application (SLDCADA). SLDCADA is an unclassified, web-based Government Off-the-Shelf time-and-attendance and labor-reporting information technology application that supports a large Navy, Marine Corps, and Executive Office of the President user community and directly supports payroll and labor-distribution operations. SLDCADA provides a single input screen via a single sign on capability utilizing Common Access Card/Public Key Infrastructure (CAC/PKI)-based login functionality. SLDCADA currently provides T&A capabilities and labor reporting services to more than 60,000 users. This will be a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) task order with a one-year base award and four one-year option periods.

title: USAFA TR Commercial Lodging Services
description: See Attachments Solicitation FA700027Q0010 has been amended on 19 Nov 2026 Amendment 1 Description The purpose of this amendment is to clarify Government requirements, add FAR 52.219-14 to Attachment 4 � Provisions and Clauses, and update the evaluation criteria. All previously uploaded attachments have been deleted and replaced with updated versions. Offerors MUST use the updated attachments when submitting their quotations. The following major changes have been incorporated into the solicitation package: 1. Updates to the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation: Third-Party Offerors (Brokers): Language has been added to Factor 1 clarifying that third-party management companies are permitted to quote, but they must explicitly identify the physical hotel property, provide a signed Letter of Commitment from that facility if it is not registered as a small business in the System for Award Management at sam.gov, and prove compliance with the Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14). Capability Statement Additions: Offerors must now identify their dedicated Point of Contact (POC) for reservations, describe their reservation process, and affirmatively acknowledge the capability to meet a 24-hour response time. 2. Updates to the Requirement Statement (Attachment 1): Reservations & POC: Added Section 5.1, requiring a dedicated POC who must respond to authorized caller reservation requests within 24 hours. 3. Updates to Provisions and Clauses (Attachment 4): Limitations on Subcontracting: Added FAR 52.219-14 to enforce the 50% pass-through limit for small business set-asides. Offerors are advised to carefully review all updated attachments in their entirety prior to submitting a quote.

It maintains a diverse fleet of over 227,000 vehicles, including light, medium, and heavy-duty vehicles, to include sedans, SUVs, vans, trucks, buses, ambulances, and law enforcement vehicles. Vehicles range from gasoline and diesel fueled vehicles to alternative fuel vehicles (AFVs), such as electric vehicles (EVs) to low-speed electric vehicles (LSEV�s) and non-powered vehicles and trailers. Nationally, GSA Fleet orders and receives on average 30,000+ vehicles from suppliers annually. As GSA Fleet is responsible for the disposition of its vehicles, it then remarkets and sells the used vehicles across the United States and its territories, Japan, and Europe. Its vehicles are sold under the exchange/sale authority of 41 CFR 102-39. This authority aims to expedite the disposal process and maximize proceeds in the most cost-effective manner to the U.S. taxpayer. To achieve this objective, GSA Fleet currently sells its used vehicles via live and online auctions worldwide, leveraging its contracts with commercial vendors to carry out all auction-related services. These auctions must adhere to all legal and regulatory requirements.
